events.title: Savonarola Burned at the Stake in Florence
events.description: The fiery Dominican friar Girolamo Savonarola was executed in Florence. He had led the city after the Medici fell, and he was known for his 'Bonfire of the Vanities' and his fierce sermons against corruption. He was hanged and burned in the public square.
events.significance: His fall showed how quickly religious and political fortunes could turn in Renaissance Italy. His story is still a classic warning about mixing zealotry with power.

events.title: The Defenestration of Prague
events.description: Angry Protestant nobles confronted two Catholic royal governors in Prague Castle. They threw the governors and their secretary out of a high window. All three survived the fall.
events.significance: The incident helped set off the Thirty Years' War. That war devastated much of Central Europe and reshaped its political order.

events.title: Captain William Kidd Is Hanged in London
events.description: The Scottish-born sailor William Kidd was hanged at Execution Dock on the Thames. He had been convicted of piracy and of murdering a crewman. Some people believed he had been made a scapegoat for political reasons.
events.significance: Kidd became one of history's best-known pirates. His legend fed stories of buried treasure that still shape popular culture.

events.title: South Carolina Ratifies the U.S. Constitution
events.description: South Carolina became the eighth state to approve the new Constitution of the United States. The vote brought the young republic one step closer to the nine states needed to put the framework into effect.
events.significance: The ratification added momentum to the national government. It also helped establish the constitutional system that endures today.

events.title: Bonnie and Clyde Are Killed in a Louisiana Ambush
events.description: Outlaws Bonnie Parker and Clyde Barrow were shot dead by law officers on a rural road in Louisiana. They had spent about two years on a robbery and murder spree across the central United States during the Great Depression.
events.significance: The ambush ended one of the most notorious crime sprees of the era. The pair became enduring figures in American folklore and film.
